title: 4 Palestinians Killed, 16 Wounded Across Gaza on Day 944 — 215th Consecutive Day of Ceasefire Violations
detail: Israeli forces killed four Palestinians and wounded 16 others across Gaza on May 12, 2026 — Day 944 of the war and the second day of Israel's renewed military campaign authorized on May 10. The deaths were confirmed by Gaza health sources and IMEMC as the 215th consecutive day of violations under the nominal October 2025 ceasefire framework. Named victims: Mohammad Annaba, a father of two with a pregnant wife, was killed by an Israeli shell strike near the Bani Suheila roundabout in eastern Khan Younis; Mohammad Khader Totah was shot by sniper fire in the Zeitoun neighborhood of Gaza City; and Munir Eid Mohammad al-Jatli (age 30) and Alaa Ibrahim Salim Ayad (age 31) were found dead near the al-Shuhada Junction south of Gaza City after more than 12 hours on the ground. Attack types included artillery shell strikes, sniper fire, and naval artillery from Israeli warships offshore. Cumulative deaths since the October 11, 2025 ceasefire announcement: 856 killed, 2,463 wounded. Total Palestinian deaths since October 7, 2023 now stand at approximately 72,740+.

title: IDF Kfir Brigade Spots and Eliminates Hamas Nukhba Operatives in Gaza Airstrike on Day 2 of Renewed Campaign
detail: The IDF reported on May 12, 2026 that ground troops from the Kfir Infantry Brigade operating inside Gaza identified Hamas Nukhba (elite force) operatives during Day 2 of the renewed military campaign and called in an Israeli Air Force airstrike that killed them. Nukhba fighters are the Hamas special operations forces responsible for leading the October 7, 2023 attacks including the breaches of kibbutz perimeter fences and the Nova music festival massacre. The IDF has maintained a standing targeting priority for Nukhba survivors since October 7. The strike is part of a broader pattern of targeted killing operations conducted simultaneously with large-scale ground activity — on May 4, the IDF had killed Ans Muhammad Ibrahim Hamed, a Nukhba commander who led part of the Nova music festival raid (where 378 were killed). The Kfir Brigade is one of several infantry units that Israeli authorities said would be deployed in the renewed offensive. The IDF said all strikes were conducted within areas declared as operational zones under the renewed war authorization.

title: Gaza Humanitarian System Faces Acute Pressure on Day 2 of Renewed War; Aid Corridors Threatened
detail: As Israel's renewed military campaign entered its second day on May 12, 2026, UN OCHA and humanitarian organizations warned of growing pressure on Gaza's already-decimated humanitarian infrastructure. The OCHA May 7 situation report documented that 68% of Gaza's population was burning waste for fuel due to gas shortages, a methane fire at the Firas Market dumpsite on May 1 had ignited a blaze reaching 14-meter waste heaps, and 470,000 cubic meters of waste had accumulated in southern Gaza. Weekly health services were reaching approximately 370,100 people — less than 18% of Gaza's pre-war population. Only 110 health service points had been established or restored since the October 2025 ceasefire, with 196 medical evacuations in the most recent week (92 children). Food rations covered only 75% of minimum caloric needs as of May 2026, down from 100% in January 2026. The 2026 UN Flash Appeal of $4.1 billion remained under 10% funded. OCHA noted that Israeli forces closed all aid corridors following Operation Epic Fury (the US-Israel conflict with Iran), with only Kerem Shalom crossing subsequently reopened. Unexploded ordnance from the resumed military operations had already contributed to 98 accidents, 246 injuries, and 49 deaths from ERW since the October 2025 ceasefire began. Chatham House analysts warned that the Iran war had drawn international attention away from Gaza, leaving Palestinian civilians with reduced global advocacy.

media.caption: UN OCHA May 7 humanitarian situation report: 68% of Gaza burning waste for fuel, waste heaps 14 meters high, health services reaching under 18% of population
